---
title: "Implementer"
description: "Turns an approved issue into a pull request: Claude Code writes the change, checks and reviewers look at it, you decide."
---

The implementer is the last step of the issue flow:
[triage](issue-triage.qmd) writes a spec of a bug or an idea, you approve
it with the label `bot-proceed`, the [label check](issue-label-check.qmd)
makes sure only you can, and the implementer turns the spec into a pull
request. It runs [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com) on your Claude
subscription, from a **private runner repository** that holds the token,
one issue at a time.

::: {.callout-important}
## You decide
Bots never close issues and never merge. The pull request says `Refs #n`;
change it to `Closes #n` once the work is done. Disclosure control is
decided by people: the implementer follows the spec's choice, and its
pull request shows what leaves the server so you can check it.
:::

## How a run goes

1. **Pick:** the oldest approved issue (`bot-proceed`, not yet running) of
   the target repositories. The approval is checked again: set by a login
   in `allowed-logins`, the spec unchanged since. The issue gets
   `bot-in-progress`.
2. **Write:** Claude Code works on a branch `agent-suggest/<type>/issue-<n>`
   in a sandbox (only package repositories and GitHub are reachable, no
   writing token). It makes the change, tests and documentation, and
   commits with `Refs #n`.
3. **Check:** R CMD check with the tests.
4. **Review:** a maintainability reviewer and a disclosure reviewer read
   the change; they only read. Failing checks, clear problems and changes
   beyond the spec's disclosure choice go back to the writer, for up to
   two correction rounds. Matters of taste stay comments.
5. **Publish:** on a clean machine that never ran the agent, after
   checking the approval once more: a pull request into the target's
   branch with the summary, the disclosure review, the reviewers' open
   points and the checks. A failed attempt becomes a draft pull request.

The issue's labels show where it stands:

| State | Labels |
|---|---|
| waiting | `bot-proceed` |
| running | `bot-proceed`, `bot-in-progress` |
| done | `bot-completed` |
| failed | `bot-failed` (a draft pull request and a comment) |
| needs your decision | `bot-needs-input` (a comment with the question) |

To retry, set `bot-proceed` again. After `bot-needs-input`, answer in a
comment: a new triage updates the spec, then approve again.

**Subscription limits:** at a 5-hour limit the issue keeps its approval and
its place; a timer in the target repository (`implementer-timer.yml`)
waits for the reset and starts the runner again. A weekly limit pauses
the runner until the next approval or a manual start.

## Setting it up

1. **A private runner repository** (e.g. `your-login/agent-runner`) with
   the caller below and the log caller, and the secrets
   `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (`claude setup-token`), `APP_CLIENT_ID` and
   `APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
2. **The GitHub App** of your bots, installed on the target repositories
   (contents, pull requests and issues: read and write) and on the runner
   repository (actions: read and write).
3. **In each target repository:** the [label check](issue-label-check.qmd)
   with `runner-repository` set, [triage](issue-triage.qmd), the timer
   caller below, and the labels.
